selected.title: Small businesses fighting to stay open amid 'insidious cost creep'
selected.summary: Small business owners hit with rising costs will no longer be able to add surcharges on card payments from October 1. One operator in regional South Australia has described it as an "insidious cost creep".
selected.why: New ban prohibiting small businesses from adding card payment surcharges starting October 1 alters payments policy.
selected.fullText: Small businesses struggle with rising costs as changes in card surcharge payments loom - ABC News Skip to main content Skip to news navigation, settings and search Explore the ABC news iview listen Loading ABC News News Home Small businesses struggle with rising costs as changes in card surcharge payments loom Share Share article Small businesses struggle with rising costs as changes in card surcharge payments loom By Liz Rymill and Becc Bird ABC South East SA Topic: Small Businesses Posted Wed 9 Sep 2026 at 6:30am Wed 9 Sep 2026 at 6:30am Wed 9 Sep 2026 at 6:30am Francene Martin says she did not have one customer during a Sunday trading day. ( Supplied: Francene Martin ) In short: Small business owners in rural and regional communities say they are under constant pressure from the rising costs of doing business. One in eight cafes has closed in Australia in 2026, with payment defaults also rising nationally for the third consecutive month according to CreditorWatch. What's next? From October 1, businesses will no longer be able to add a surcharge on card payments, with some small businesses electing to go "cash only" or be forced to increase charges for some items. abc.net.au/news/rising-cost-of-business-challenging-country-towns-surcharge/107116412 Link copied Share Share article In the town of Keith, a natural halfway point between Melbourne and Adelaide along the Dukes Highway, Sunday afternoon draws to an end. The main street of the agricultural town, home to a population of about 1,400 people, is quiet, as residents and travellers finish the day. Clothing shop owner Francene Martin turns the sign on her store Retail Therapy to "Closed". Today, she has not made a single sale. Francene Martin says she feels "constant pressure" from mega competitors like Amazon, Temu and Shein. ( Supplied: Francene Martin ) Across the country, countless small businesses from clothing retailers to cafes are counting the rising cost of doing business. "I was quite despondent," Ms Martin said. " I've been in the town 16 years, and even with a 50 per cent off sale, I didn't make a single cent. " Cost creep 'crippling' for small operators Across the border, in a rust-red brick heritage schoolhouse building in Ballarat, one of Victoria's largest regional centres, Prey cafe operations and social media manager Frazer Wyley posted online about the issue. reason: Payment surcharge ban creates genuine policy tradeoff: consumer protection vs. small business viability. Defensible positions exist on both sides with measurable consequences.
angle: Banning card surcharges protects consumers but will harm small businesses more than large competitors who can absorb costs.
